title: New columns

cells.text: Analysts often work out new numbers from existing columns, like the total including the tip. This lesson shows how to add your own columns.

cells.prompt: Press Run to load the deliveries table.
cells.code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("deliveries.csv")
df.head()

cells.text: To make a new column, give it a name in square brackets and store a value in it with `=`: `df["with_tip"] = df["total"] + df["tip"]`. pandas does the maths **row by row**, for every row at once.

cells.prompt: Press Run to add a with_tip column, then show it next to the total and tip.
Ben left no tip, so his tip is NaN (empty). What is his with_tip? Pick one, then press Run.

cells.text: Maths with an empty value gives an empty result, because pandas can't add a number it doesn't have. You'll learn how to fill in missing values in Level 3.

cells.prompt: Replace ___ with the divide sign to make per_minute, the dollars per minute of delivery, then press Run.

cells.text: Those numbers have lots of decimals. Wrap the maths in round brackets and add `.round(2)` to keep 2 decimal places: `(df["total"] / df["minutes"]).round(2)`.

cells.prompt: Press Run to remake per_minute with 2 decimals.
Your turn: add a column tip_percent, which is the tip as a percent of the total (tip ÷ total × 100), rounded to 1 decimal. Then show the customer and tip_percent columns.
hints: Wrap df["tip"] / df["total"] * 100 in round brackets, then add .round(1). On the second line, pick the 2 columns.

cells.text: New columns work with everything you already know. For example, you can filter on minutes and then show a new column.

cells.prompt: Last one: add a column hours (minutes ÷ 60, rounded to 2 decimals). Then show the customer and hours columns, only for deliveries that took more than 45 minutes.
hints: Line 1 makes the column like the cell above. Line 2 filters df["minutes"] > 45, then picks the 2 columns.

recap: df["new"] = ... adds a column, with the maths done row by row. Maths with NaN gives NaN. Use (maths).round(2) to round.
